rationale: Joint replacement of both c10d::allreduce_ dispatch sites of the DDP gradient sync (group f833b57a373d8262a384, 12 buckets of 7,087,872 fp32 elements; group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0, 1 bucket of 39,385,344 elements) with a symmetric per-call host-side readiness rendezvous followed by the unchanged parent op. Measured decomposition (inputs/observations, revision 63ad2b21): the objective (per-rank sum of NCCL kernel durations, max over ranks, median of 3 profiled reps) has a transport floor of ~62.3-63.5 ms - rank 1's baseline sums are 63.62/63.79/63.66 ms, matching the clean isolated calibration of the identical ops (3.56/3.65 ms per small bucket, 19.49/19.64 ms for the large one), and the nsys run put rank 0 at 62.46 ms - while rank 0's baseline objective (93.52/94.49/110.06 ms) carries ~31 ms of excess that execution_timeline-1221e205 localizes entirely to early-arrival spin charged into kernel durations: the first collective (seq21) ran 14.04 ms on rank 0 vs 3.62 ms on rank 1 (rank 0 launched ~10.5 ms early), and every later kernel stayed within ~90 us lockstep at the floor; resources.json shows the same concentration in the intrusive run (seq21 = 114.4 ms on rank 0) and the skew direction flips between runs (nsys run: rank 1 sum 241 ms), so the remedy must be symmetric. Mechanism: before dispatching each parent allreduce_, both ranks publish a monotonic arrival counter on an 8-byte /dev/shm page and the earlier rank waits on the CPU until the peer arrives, then both call the parent (torch 2.13 routes ProcessGroup::allreduce through the dispatcher op c10d::allreduce_, ProcessGroup.hpp:246, so the reducer's calls are intercepted exactly as discovery recorded them and the parent's (Tensor[], Work) return is passed through unmodified - the same pattern discovery's CaptureMode already exercised). The peer wait therefore moves out of NCCL kernel durations into host time; no NCCL kernel, no gloo collective and no CUDA work is added inside timing, the op sequence, bucket views (gradient_as_bucket_view=True), payloads, process group and completion boundary are untouched, so gradients stay bitwise identical (2-rank fp32 addition is commutative and the summed operands are unchanged) and the exact cross-rank replica check, global-batch gradient check, +1 negative control and parameter checks are unaffected. Step-time neutrality: the baseline already ends with both ranks equal (144.63/144.54 ms vs the 151.86 ms budget); the early rank merely pauses on the host until the pacer rank reaches the same call, after which both execute identical remaining work, so step_ms is expected to stay at ~144-146 ms; the compute/communication overlap lost during the relocated wait is bounded by the same pacer argument because the late rank was never overlapping ahead of that point. Expected objective ~63-65 ms (median of 3 reps, both ranks at the transport floor), i.e. roughly a 30-33% reduction from 94.49 ms; no per-byte wire-time reduction is claimed - the ~8 GB/s logical rate over the SHM/direct transport (peer_access 0 in both directions) is a transport property and all 497,759,232 bytes still cross the same NCCL ring ops. Robustness: the rendezvous is bounded by a configurable budget (default 1000 ms, far above the largest observed 48 ms in-step skew and the ~180 ms nsys-inflated case), after which the call still dispatches the parent; two consecutive timeouts permanently disable the rendezvous (bounded added latency, correctness unchanged); installation failure (no /dev/shm, no gloo control group, unreachable peer page) falls back to pure parent passthrough reported as the setup-parent route. The readiness exchange never touches the NCCL group and never creates a process group: the existing gloo control group is used only during installation (outside timing) to agree on the page name, matching its sanctioned out-of-timer role; per-step counters are monotonic per process, so warmup, clean repeats, the 3 profiled diagnostic reps, quality runs and continuous steps all work without reset logic, and reset()/state semantics are not touched. Both call IDs receive the shared handler, preserving collective participation on both ranks; coverage sees 12 and 1 replacement invocations per step plus the corresponding parent invocations through context.references.

setup_work.when: installation only (build), outside every timed or profiled region
steps: One gloo all_gather_object plus one gloo barrier on the adapter's existing control group (state['control_group']) to agree on a random 32-hex-char token; no new process group is created and the NCCL group is untouched.
Rank 0 creates an 8-byte file under /dev/shm named with the token (two int32 arrival counters zero-initialized); all ranks mmap it read-write after the barrier.
One liveness probe handshake (bounded at 5 s) verifies cross-process visibility; on failure the channel is dropped and every call uses the parent path (setup-parent route).
An atexit hook unlinks the page; the mapping is held for the process lifetime.
setup_work.memory: No CUDA allocations, no parameter transforms, no retained device pools; retained host state is one 8-byte tmpfs mapping plus one file descriptor. framework.peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle peaks are unaffected.
setup_work.tunable_parameters: sync_wait_budget_ms (default 1000, legal 250/500/1000/2000) only bounds how long a rank may wait for a late peer before degrading to the parent path; it never changes workload, sampling, data or thresholds.

quality_risks: Interception depends on dispatcher-level routing of the reducer's collectives (c10d::allreduce_ with the two observed contiguous fp32 signatures, phase run, project-level parent), which is exactly what the discovery artifacts recorded; if a live signature ever failed to match, the framework's mode falls back to the parent for that call, keeping outputs correct at baseline metric.

The host-side wait runs on the reducer's calling thread; it is bounded by the budget and disabled after two consecutive timeouts, so worst-case added latency is about 2x budget once per process; under normal operation the wait equals the peer arrival skew that previously inflated kernel durations.
If a profiled repetition exhibits arrival skew larger than the budget, that repetition degrades toward the baseline value while remaining correct; the objective uses the median of 3 repetitions.

Step_ms has 7.2 ms of headroom (144.63 -> 151.86 ms); the relocated wait is wall-time neutral by the pacer-rank argument, but a pathological run that loses more overlap than the skew it removes could consume part of it; no mechanism is known by which the change increases total work.

Numerical outputs are unchanged by construction (identical ops, operands and order); the bitwise cross-rank replica check (atol=0.0, rtol=0.0) and the reference gradient check would detect any deviation, and no fallback route alters values.

Installation-time gloo rendezvous relies on the control group being present on both ranks (adapter.prepare creates it); asymmetric installation would stall until the group timeout inside setup and then fall back to parent passthrough without affecting correctness.

params.name: sync_wait_budget_ms
params.description: Maximum host-side wait per allreduce dispatch for the peer's arrival before degrading to the parent path; 1000 ms covers the largest observed in-step skew (48 ms profiled, ~180 ms under nsys) with margin.
